They are not comfortable. I do not like them. But I need them. I am a tawny owl. I eat what I catch. I do not chew. I swallow whole.

My home is the hollow in the old oak. It is dry and deep, and I have made it warm with my feathers. The entrance is small, just wide enough for me to squeeze through. I can hear the wind in the branches and the leaves rustling. The hollow is dark, but I do not mind. I am safe here. I have a mate, and we have our own home. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The wood is my world, and I know every branch and root. I have raised my young there, and I will stay until the cold comes. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

A hollow in the old oak, the one by the stream. The bark is rough and the leaves fall in autumn. I have a mate, and we have a hollow. That is all I know of home. The rest is the meadow, the stream, the lane, the road, and the lights.

My home is the hollow in the old oak. It is dry and deep, and I have made it my own. The oak is near the stream, where the meadow meets the wood. I have been here for many years, and the hollow is warm in the winter and cool in the summer. I have raised my young here, and I have watched the seasons change. The hollow is my safe place, and I return to it every night. I have no other home.

It is in the ash tree at the edge of the wood. I have been there since the leaves fell. It is a hollow, deep and dry, with a narrow entrance. I can see the meadow from there, and the lane, and the stream. I can hear the road from the hollow, and the cars that pass. I have a nest of feathers and down in the hollow, and I have a mate.
